header.running_head: The Marriages of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.text: A third narration quotes the du'aa of Rasulullaah ﷺ as:

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ بَارِكْ فِيْهِمَا وَبَارِكْ عَلَيْهِمَا وَبَارِكْ لَهُمَا فِيْ بِنَائِهِمَا وَبَارِكْ فِيْ نَسْلِهِمَا
blocks.text: "O Allaah! Bless the two of them, shower Your blessings on them, bless them in their consummation and bless them in their progeny." [^1]
Yet another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added:

Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) narrates that after Hadhrat Faatima (RA) was married to Hadhrat Ali (RA), all that they saw in her house was a straw mat spread out on the ground, a pillow stuffed with the bark of a palm tree, an earthen jug and an earthen mug. (On the night of the marriage) Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a message saying, "Do nothing" or "Do not get close to your wife until I come." When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived, he asked, "Is my brother here?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ forged bonds of brotherhood between the Sahabah (RA), he forged his brotherhood with Hadhrat Ali (RA). Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA), a pious woman who was an Abyssinian and the mother of Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) asked in surprise, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! He is your brother and you have married your daughter to him?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "This (marriage) can take place (despite this type of brotherhood), O Ummu Ayman."

Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for a container of water, uttered some words and then passed his hands over the chest and face of Hadhrat Ali (RA). He then called Hadhrat Faatima (RA) who stood by him shivering in her shawl out of modesty. Rasulullaah ﷺ sprinkled some of the water on her and also uttered some words. He then said to her, "I have not failed you in my duty to get you married to the family member I love most." Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) narrates further. She says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then noticed a figure behind the curtain or behind the door and asked, 'Who is that?' 'Asmaa,' I replied. 'Asmaa bint Umays?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. 'Yes, O Rasulullaah ﷺ,' I confirmed. He then asked, 'Have you come to be of service to Rasulullaah ﷺ (and his family)?' 'Yes,' I replied, 'because a young girl must have a family woman with her on her first night to take care of anything she might need.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then made such a wonderful du'aa for me that it is the one deed that I have most hope in (to deliver me to salvation in the Aakhirah). Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to Ali (RA), 'Look after you wife' and as he left, he continued making du'aa for them until he disappeared in his rooms." [^3]
